According to the DPDP Rules 2025, a Data Fiduciary can verify the identity of a parent before processing a child's data in the following ways:

1. By checking reliable details of identity and age of the parent available with the Data Fiduciary (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 10(1)(a)).
2. By verifying details of identity and age, voluntarily provided by the parent (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 10(1)(b)(i)).
3. By using a virtual token mapped to such details, which is issued by an authorised entity (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 10(1)(b)(ii)).

These methods are outlined in Rule 10 of the DPDP Rules 2025, which came into force on 13 November 2025.

According to Rule 8(3) of the DPDP Rules 2025, a Data Fiduciary must retain, in respect of any processing of personal data undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, such personal data, associated traffic data, and other logs of the processing for a minimum period of one year from the date of such processing. After this period, the Data Fiduciary shall cause such personal data and logs to be erased, unless further retention is required for compliance with any other law for the time being in force or notified by the Government.

This requirement is stated in both the final version of Rule 8 (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 8) and the draft version (Draft DPDP Rules 2025, draft r. 8).

This is stated in Rule 13(4) of the DPDP Rules 2025 (DPDP Rules 2025, r. 13(4)).
